test_title: SSC MTS (2022) Official Paper (Held On: 04 May 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Capacities of six tanks A, B, C, D, E and F are compared. No two tanks have same capacity. Capacity of D is more than F and C. Capacity of A is less than only B. Which of the following sequence about their capacities can be correct?

I. A > D > E

II. C > F > E
solution:
Given: Six tanks A, B, C, D, E and F are compared. 

No two tanks have same capacity. 

The capacity of D is more than F and C. 

D > F > C

or 

D > C > F

The capacity of A is less than only B.

B > A > __ > __ > __ > __

After combining the statements, we have 8 possible cases;

Case I: B > A > D > F > C > E

Case II: B > A > D > C > F > E

Case III: B > A > E > D > C > F 

Case IV: B > A > E > D > F > C

Case V: B > A > D > F > E > C

Case VI: B > A > D > C > E > F

Case VII: B > A > D > E > C > F 

Case VIII: B > A > D > E > F > C

Now, checking the given sequence:

I. A > D > E - True (From case I)

II. C > F > E - True (From Case II)

Hence, the correct answer is "**Option (4)**".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e085a7f17645c801966c030eb44d69fae944b96fdb4c4077f5fba1bc2c24bc71.png] __Mistake Points__

We have reviewed the question and found it to be correct. The task is to determine whether the given sequence is "POSSIBLE" or not.

After considering all possibilities, we conclude that both sequences are possible. This means that both sequences can occur, but neither is definitely true.
